properties.name: Anthony built xrt-mcp the same evening (2026-09-16, /home/ajs7/project/xrt-mcp: nine tools, a typed BeamlineSpec instead of executed Python, its own reflow2 design of 68 nodes) and asked for xrt-demo — a light trial on this box that tunes xrt-mcp and demonstrates the reflow2 pairing; brief written at /home/ajs7/project/xrt-demo/demo.md for /genesis
properties.statement: Anthony, 2026-09-16: "I built out the xrt-mcp at /home/ajs7/project/xrt-mcp. /brainstorm a project at /home/ajs7/project/xrt-demo that will: 1) fine-tune the newly developed but unused xrt-mcp and 2) demonstrate some useful demonstration that exercises the partnership between reflow2 and xrt-demo. Remember, this machine is not powerful — so the test can't be too intensive (we can save that for my work computer)." WHAT xrt-mcp IS (read from its README and code): xrt 2.0.0b1 behind the MCP Python SDK 2.x; nine tools — crystal_at_energy, crystal_energy_range, mirror_cutoff, undulator_harmonics (reference, no trace) and list_beamlines, load_beamline, trace_beamline, beam_image, scan_element (whole-beamline); a beamline is sent as a typed pydantic BeamlineSpec (source + elements: aperture, DCM Si(111/220/311/333), flat/toroidal mirror with coating and pitch, screen; positions in metres along the beam) and the server builds the xrt objects itself — it never executes agent-written Python, which answers the arbitrary-code risk recorded on the CAD-pairing idea; four templates, one geometric-source "fast" variant (seconds) and undulator variants (20–60 s per trace, minutes per scan); flux is null for a geometric source rather than a made-up number; stateless; limits stated honestly (four element types, ray tracing only, templates plausible not as-built, vertical deflection only). It has its own reflow2 design: 11 requirements accepted, 9 capabilities (6 verified), req:demo-for-nsls-ii. THE BRIEF written for /genesis at xrt-demo/demo.md: a hard x-ray endstation from the nsls2-hard-xray template at 9 keV; four requirements (spot ≤ 30×5 µm, bandwidth ≤ 2 eV, transmission ≥ 0.5 %, flux stated but UNVERIFIABLE on this box because the geometric source carries no flux weight — the design must say so); a compute budget (≤ 20 000 rays, ≤ 60 s, no undulator, no GPU here); the artifact standard is the BeamlineSpec JSON with trace_beamline as its checker; a per-kind unit system (eV, m, µm, mrad, mm, ph/s, W); every number computed by an xrt-mcp call with provenance; two changes (mirror pitch 3.0→3.5 mrad, slit 1.0→0.5 mm) recorded and propagated BEFORE re-tracing; rough edges logged into xrt-mcp's own design with /log-issue. Quality attribute: testability. .mcp.json for xrt-demo names the xrt server (the xrt-mcp venv python with PYTHONPATH). This is the same figure as bhome/IfcMCP one domain over, and the first trial where the tool is his own.
